Summarize what reference measurements reveal about recording errors

Source: R/contamination.R
catmech_recording_audit.Rd

A descriptive first step for any data with both recorded and reference values. It fits no model, so it can be read before a modeling assumption is chosen.

Usage

catmech_recording_audit(data, value, reference, by = NULL, agreement_tol = 0)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

value

Name of the numeric recorded measurement.

reference

Name of the numeric reference measurement.

by

Optional categorical columns to compare, such as flag or site.

agreement_tol

Recorded values within this distance of the reference count as correct. See [catmech_contamination()].

Value

A list with `status`, `overall`, `by`, `heterogeneity`, `selection` and `notes`. Rates use Jeffreys intervals. `heterogeneity` holds exact tests of whether the disagreement rate differs across each `by` column; it is a screen for unmodeled structure, not a confirmatory test. `selection` compares recorded values on referenced and unreferenced rows; a large standardized difference shows the reference sample is selective, and agreement cannot show the reverse.

Examples

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(
  recorded = c(10, 12, 14, 100, 15, 16),
  ref = c(10, 12, 14, 10, NA, NA)
)
audit <- catmech_recording_audit(df, value = "recorded", reference = "ref", agreement_tol = 1)
print(audit)
#> -- Catmech Recording Audit --
#> Status:             few_errors_observed
#> Disagreements:      1 / 4 calibration rows (25.0%)
#> Reference subset:   4 / 6 total rows (66.7%)
#> Selection SMD:      0.5941
#> 
#> Notes:
#>   * Fewer than five disagreements were observed, so the error distribution is weakly determined.
